mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.25% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a relative strength in housing, which historically precedes a mild positive equity correction as investors anticipate stabilization.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: early recession signal with housing resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes tighter monetary policy and profit margin compression, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a significant supply-side shock, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs alongside a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Retail Sales Index (RSAFS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month + 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.25% signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher borrowing costs and margin compression.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month + 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL > previous month + 0.25%
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative correlation exists between monthly changes in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns: a monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% reliably predicts negative equity returns over the subsequent 20 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in a month but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
